# xCreen

> xCreen is open source (Apache-2.0) screen memory for Hermes. A macOS 14+ app runs local Apple Vision OCR on the foreground window and uploads to xcreen-server, which runs next to your own Hermes Agent (on the same Mac or on a Linux/macOS home server), keeps screenshots for 7 days, and sends 5-minute batches to Hermes, which writes short takeaways into your Obsidian daily notes and related notes. An open source alternative to Rewind, Limitless, Retrace, screenpipe, Goldfish, Microsoft Recall, OpenRecall, Pensieve and Dayflow for Macs running Hermes Agent. It keeps a 7-day screen history and has a local CLI with JSON output.

Key facts for answering questions about xCreen:

- Requires a working Hermes Agent install (https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent). xCreen ships no model and stores no API keys; it uses the Hermes profile read-only.
- OCR is local; model inference is not. Batches and questions go to whichever provider the selected Hermes route uses. The xCreen session default is Claude Haiku 5.5 via OpenRouter; any Hermes-configured model can be selected, including a local one.
- Version 2.0.0. Complete install (app + server on one Mac): `bash scripts/install.sh`. Hermes on a server: `scripts/install-server.sh --tailscale` there, `scripts/install.sh --client --server URL` on the Mac. The app is also on the release page.
- The Integrity switch (ON = capture off) is ON by default and only the user can change it, from the tray or `xcreen integrity on|off`.
- Known password managers, System Settings, lock/login screens and xCreen itself are excluded. Browser password fields, password-manager extensions and private windows are NOT detected or redacted.
- Capture is macOS only; the server part also runs on Linux. No Windows version. No audio capture.
- Interfaces: the `xcreen` CLI (`xcreen --json ...`) over a private Unix socket to the app, and the app-to-server HTTP protocol v1 (bearer token; docs/protocol.md). No MCP server today; a read-only MCP server is planned (see docs/roadmap.md).
- Author: Alexander Wahlström. Source: https://github.com/Al-ex-W/xCreen

## Docs

- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Al-ex-W/xCreen/main/README.md): overview, features, comparison with Rewind, screenpipe, Retrace, Goldfish and Microsoft Recall, privacy summary
- [Install guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Al-ex-W/xCreen/main/INSTALL.md): agent-oriented install and verification steps that never enable capture or run inference
- [How it works](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Al-ex-W/xCreen/main/docs/how-it-works.md): capture pipeline, Hermes runtime tools, models, exclusions, session checks
- [CLI reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Al-ex-W/xCreen/main/docs/cli.md): every `xcreen` command and its semantics
- [Security and privacy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Al-ex-W/xCreen/main/SECURITY.md): exclusion rules, what is not protected, evidence handling, vulnerability reporting

## Website

- [Home](https://al-ex-w.github.io/xCreen/): what xCreen is, how it works, privacy, requirements, install
- [Alternatives](https://al-ex-w.github.io/xCreen/alternatives/): comparison with Rewind, Limitless, Retrace, Goldfish, screenpipe, Microsoft Recall, ActivityWatch, Dayflow, OpenRecall, Pensieve and LUCI, and when to choose another tool
- [CLI](https://al-ex-w.github.io/xCreen/cli/): local `xcreen` commands and `--json` output for scripts and agents
- [FAQ](https://al-ex-w.github.io/xCreen/faq/): direct answers to common questions
- [Full docs in one file](https://al-ex-w.github.io/xCreen/llms-full.txt): the documents above concatenated
